strategy.summary: cartTotal(items, {coupon}) in src/cart.js prices a cart: bulk 10% off at the item-count threshold, SAVE5 coupon after it (floored at $0), unknown coupons throw, $4.99 shipping below $50 of discounted goods, empty cart free. Unit tests in Vitest prove each rule and its boundaries. Reading the code shows bulkDiscount uses `> BULK_THRESHOLD`, so a cart of exactly 10 items gets no discount, against AC1; that case is kept as an expected failure and reported as a defect.
inScope: cartTotal, bulkDiscount behaviour in src/cart.js via its exported API
outOfScope: UI/checkout pages (none exist in the repo)
assumptions: Shipping still applies when a coupon brings goods to $0 on a non-empty cart (AC3: goods under $50 pay $4.99).
Coupon codes are matched exactly (case-sensitive), as the code does.
Tests go in a new file test/cart-total.test.js beside the existing test/cart.test.js, importing from ../src/cart.js like it.
openQuestions: Should coupon codes be case-insensitive (e.g. 'save5')? The code refuses them; not tested.

risks.description: Off-by-one at the 10-item threshold (code uses > instead of >=)
risks.mitigation: TC1 asserts exactly 10 items across lines gets the discount (expected failure, defect recorded).

risks.description: Coupon applied before the bulk discount, or free-shipping judged before discounts
risks.mitigation: TC4 and TC8 use amounts where the wrong order gives a different total.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A cart with 10 or more items in total (sum of line quantities) gets 10% off its subtotal; fewer than 10 gets none.
Coupon SAVE5 takes $5 off after the bulk discount, goods never below $0; any other coupon code is refused with an error.
Shipping is free when goods after discounts are $50 or more, otherwise $4.99; an empty cart costs $0.

defects.title: Cart of exactly 10 items gets no bulk discount
defects.description: AC1: 10 or more items get 10% off. src/cart.js bulkDiscount uses `itemCount(items) > BULK_THRESHOLD` (should be >=), so a 10-item cart (4+6 at $10) is charged 100 instead of 90.
defects.evidence: cartTotal([{price:10,quantity:4},{price:10,quantity:6}]) returns 100; test marked it.fails passes, i.e. the toBe(90) assertion fails.

review.standard: Assert the one outcome the app produces / List a criterion on a case only when that case's assertions would fail if the criterion weren't met (AC1: quantities added up across lines)
review.summary: The only test with more than one line is the it.fails TC1. it.fails passes on any failure, so no passing test shows that itemCount adds up quantities across lines; every other bulk case (TC2, TC3, TC4, TC9) uses a single line.
review.failureScenario: Say itemCount regresses to counting only one line's quantity, for example `items[0]?.quantity ?? 0` or `Math.max(...quantities)`. TC3, TC4 and TC9 (one line of 12) still get the discount and pass. TC2 (one line of 9) passes. TC1 ({4},{6}) still returns 100 rather than 90, so it.fails stays green. The suite passes while AC1's 'adding up each line's quantity' is broken. The same happens if cartTotal throws, say a TypeError from a refactor: TC1 'fails' and it.fails passes. Fix: add a passing multi-line case above the threshold that the current code discounts, e.g. [{price:10,quantity:5},{price:10,quantity:6}] -> 99 (110 - 11, free shipping). That way, summing across lines is checked by a test that is not marked expected-to-fail.
